summary: Margarita Iosifovna Vorobyova-Desyatovskaya was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at St. Petersburg University (~1950–1955) and held posts at the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1956–2007) and the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (~1956–2021).
Margarita Kleibel is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Karin Preisendanz and completed her MA under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes (~2008–2010).

Margherita Serena Saccone works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She completed her doctorate under Birgit Kellner (~2007–2011) and served as a project member and researcher at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (~2011).

Maria Heim is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned her BA at Reed College (~1987–1991) and her PhD at Harvard University (~1993–1999) under Charles Hallisey. She became Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Amherst College (~2007).

Marianne Winder was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of London (until ~1953) and SOAS, held a post at the University of Nottingham (~1953–1963), and served as Keeper of the Oriental Manuscripts at the Wellcome Trust (~1964–1978).
Marie G. Wanek is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1960–1978), where she was taught by Sengaku Maeda (~1964–1968).
Marina Illich is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Columbia University (~1999–2006), where she studied under Robert A. F. Thurman.

Mario D'Amato is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1994–2000) under Paul J. Griffiths. He has held posts at Rollins College and Hampshire College (~2006).

Mario Kozah is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Cambridge under James Montgomery (~2001–2005) and held a post at the American University of Beirut (~2008).

Mario Poceski is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at UCLA (~1994–2000) under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and was appointed Assistant Professor of Buddhist Studies and Chinese Religions at the University of Florida (~2003).
Marion L. Matics is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Matics studied under doctoral supervisors Horace L. Friess and Royal W. Weiler, as well as teacher Robert A. Fowkes.

Mark A. Nathan works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He earned his PhD at UCLA (~2003–2010) under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and later served as a lecturer at the University at Buffalo (~2010).

Mark Allon is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his doctorate at St John's College, Cambridge (~1989–1994) under Kenneth Roy Norman, and later became chair of the Department of Indian Sub-Continental Studies at the University of Sydney (~2002).

Mark C. Elliott is a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He served as professor of history at the University of California, Santa Barbara (1998) and became Professor of Chinese and Inner Asian History at Harvard University (~2003).

Mark Csikszentmihalyi is a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He was an associate professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1994–2005) and became Professor of East Asian Languages and Cultures at the University of California, Berkeley (~2005).

Mark D. Griffiths studied at the University of Exeter (1987–1990). He held a post at the University of Plymouth (1990–1995) before becoming Professor of Gambling Studies at Nottingham Trent University in 1995.

Mark Juergensmeyer is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Illinois (~1958–1961), Union Theological Seminary (~1961–1965), and Columbia University (~1963–1965), and became a professor and director at UC Santa Barbara (~1989).

Mark L. Blum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held a post at the State University of New York (~1997–2002) and served as an associate professor at the University at Albany, SUNY (~2002–2012).
Mark Owen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Leeds under the doctoral supervision of Anna King and Elizabeth Stuart.

Mark S. G. Dyczkowski was an Indologist who completed his doctorate at the University of Oxford (~1975–1980) under Richard Gombrich, while also studying under traditional teachers Lakshman Joo (~1976–1991) and Kedar Raj Rajopadhyaya.
